runtime.note: structure and correctness only; no hardware timing claim

defect.summary: dispatch_complex_extract bound the raw input with a flat count/offset and no shape/stride metadata, so broadcast (stride-0) and transposed complex64 inputs were read as dense storage. Abs::eval_gpu routes here, so upstream test_fft_contiguity failed before FFT ran.
defect.root_cause: Upstream MLX 0.32.2 keeps the no-gaps `contiguous` flag set across broadcast and transposed views (flags.contiguous means gap-free, not row-major); the flat read additionally needs row_contiguous. dispatch_complex handled this with ensure_dense + fill_broadcast_transport; the extract helper had neither.

fix: dispatch_complex_extract now normalizes its input through the same ensure_dense materialization path dispatch_complex uses, gated on flags().contiguous && flags().row_contiguous. Non-row-contiguous inputs are materialized once via contiguous_copy_gpu (strided-copy engine, complex64 proven); row-contiguous views with a nonzero offset keep the existing flat-offset read. All three callers (Abs, Real, Imag) go through this one helper; Conjugate already routes through dispatch_complex.

omarchy_complex_ops_tests.note: the new case 'complex extract and abs agree on broadcast transposed and offset views' failed on Abs/Real/Imag over broadcast and transposed views; Conjugate and the offset slice already agreed

limitations: Values verified on llvmpipe; no M1/Honeykrisp run in this wave (task scope is the x86 dev box).
No shader files changed, so the glslc/glslangValidator compiler-split rule does not apply.

Broadcast inputs to Abs/Real/Imag now pay one dense materialization; a stride-carrying extract kernel would avoid the copy but was out of scope (task prefers reusing the existing materialization path over a second stride convention).
